pron.heading: Pronunciation tip
pron.final: For word end or before consonant, final consonant wey be tense or aspirated stop, s, j or ch (k-, t-, p-types and sibilants) dey sound like plain k, t or p; example na {ex}.
pron.liaison: When single or double final consonant come before particle, ending or suffix wey start with vowel (dem write am with silent first consonant), di final consonant dey sound as di start of di next syllable; example na {ex}.
pron.nasal: Final stop sound (k, t or p type) dey change to nasal sound (ng, n or m) before nasal consonant (n or m); example na {ex}.
pron.lateral: When n sound and l/r sound meet across syllable boundary, dem usually sound like l (small exceptions dey); example na {ex}.
pron.tense: After final stop sound (k, t or p type), di next plain consonant (g, d, b, s or j type) dey sound tense; example na {ex}.
pron.source: Source: Standard Pronunciation Rules of Korean, article {art} (National Institute of Korean Language).
pron.note: This tip dey explain rule. Your device voice na only to play sound; this app no dey judge your own pronunciation.
